title: Homebase error envelope
description: Every API error uses this shape. The 'code' field is the contract — clients switch on it and it never changes meaning once shipped. The 'message' field is not: rewording it, or translating it, is a compatible change. Mirrors the Error schema in api/openapi.yaml; both are validated in CI and must not diverge.

code.description: Stable machine-readable identifier, 'domain.reason'. The domain matches an API area.

message.description: One sentence for the person reading it, who does not know what a mount point is. Never contains a path, a device name, or a stack trace — those belong in 'detail'.
examples: The backup disk is not connected.

detail.description: Specifics for someone diagnosing the problem. May name paths, devices and versions. Must never contain a secret, a token or a password.

recoverable.description: Whether retrying could plausibly succeed. Distinguishes 'the disk is unplugged' from 'this request can never work'.

recovery.description: What the user can actually do about it. An error that is recoverable should say how.
examples: Reconnect the backup disk and try again.

request_id.description: Correlates this response with the logs and the audit trail.

allOf.description: A recoverable error must say how to recover from it. Reporting that a problem is fixable without saying how is worse than saying nothing.
